cells.tense: You are the one weighing what carries forward, and at this moment you are doing it well.
cells.ask: This week, go toward the one connection that still holds and say out loud what stopped carrying. One sentence, plainly. Then stay there.
cells.core:
You can look at a shared thing — a group, a friendship, a way of doing something together — and tell what is alive in it from what is only upright. That is not coldness. It is care willing to lose something in order to keep the thing honest, and it lets you stay close to people without pretending.

The work now is small and exact. As you walk into what still connects, name what you are leaving. Telling one person what stopped carrying for you is how the crossing stays yours rather than a drift. The balance costs the same thing it has cost before — saying the leaving out loud while it is happening.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell what is alive in this, and you are willing to lose what is not.
cells.verb: crossing into what still connects and leaving the rest where it stood
cells.place: the clearing after a structure built on a false premise falls

cells.tense: You are bracing for a threshold that has not arrived, writing the ending before the moment is here.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are treating as already over. Say the sentence to someone today, just that one. Let the week answer it.
cells.core:
You are standing at a door before it is a door. Conversations about this group, this friendship, this shared thing get angled toward the ending that is coming — you have already written the leaving scene and are casting people into it. That is not intuition. It is the mind pulling the clearing forward so the ground feels known.

The sentence has to stand on its own and let the week contradict it. What you are pushing for is real too — you can tell a false version of something from the one that breathes. But a threshold announced early does not make the crossing. It just makes you the one who cannot be surprised.

cells.tense: You are still on the near side of a door you walked through, and you have not said so.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you have already left, and why it stopped holding. Then answer one question they ask back.
cells.core:
This works best as standing in a shared thing and knowing what it needs, then saying so while people are still in the room. That is what is available here. What is happening instead is that something in a shared thing stopped holding for you, you stepped past it — quietly, maybe just by going silent inside it — and you have kept showing up as if you were inside it still.

The way through is not more feeling. It is clearer thinking: the part that ended for you can be put into one sentence with another person. They do not have to agree. Let them ask one thing back, and answer it.
cells.sheetLine: You stepped past a door and kept showing up as if you had not.

cells.tense: You are already letting what stopped carrying fall away, and describing it as a thing that happened on its own.
cells.ask: Pick one letting-go you have called natural, and name it once to one person. Say what it makes room for.
cells.core:
Trace where your time and attention have actually moved over these months. People and gatherings you used to be part of, you are not. That move happened, and it was yours — made quietly, without announcement. The distance opened because you opened it. The way you tell it, things simply ended up that way.

You also know what you were stepping away from, and when you mention it you mention it lightly, as though it were easy. It was not. It was the same recognition this whole thing runs on, only you have not claimed it as yours. One sentence to one person is all it takes to make the crossing yours.
cells.sheetLine: You are already walking on. The only missing part is saying it.
